intro: A partial derivative measures how fast a quantity changes when just one input changes. This branch extends the idea of a derivative (rate of change) to functions of several inputs, including the gradient, which points straight uphill.

VII.11.01.what: A partial derivative measures how the output changes when one input moves and the others stay fixed, like walking due east on a hillside.

levels.a: Holds all other inputs fixed and varies just one.
levels.b: Interprets it as the slope in one direction.
levels.c: Reads and writes the notation for partial derivatives.
levels.d: Uses the limit definition to compute one from scratch.

VII.11.02.what: Computing partial derivatives using the usual derivative rules, treating the other variables as fixed numbers.

levels.a: Finds the partial derivative with respect to x.
levels.b: Finds the partial derivative with respect to y.
levels.c: Finds partial derivatives of functions with three inputs.
levels.d: Estimates partial derivatives from a contour map.

VII.11.03.what: Taking partial derivatives again to measure how rates of change themselves change.

levels.b: Finds mixed partials, taken first in one variable then another.
levels.c: Uses the fact that the order of mixed partials usually does not matter.
levels.d: Checks whether a function satisfies the Laplace equation from physics.

VII.11.04.what: A tangent plane is the flat surface that just touches a curved surface at one point, like a sheet of paper resting on a ball.

levels.a: Learns the formula for a tangent plane.
levels.b: Finds the tangent plane at a given point.
levels.c: Finds tangent planes to level surfaces.
levels.d: Finds the line sticking straight out of the surface (the normal line).

VII.11.05.what: Using the tangent plane to estimate values of a function near a known point.

levels.a: Uses the tangent plane as an estimate of the surface.
levels.b: Approximates a function value near a known point.
levels.c: Estimates small changes in output from small changes in inputs.
levels.d: Estimates how measurement errors grow in a calculation.

VII.11.06.what: A function is differentiable at a point if it is smooth enough there to have a good tangent plane.

levels.a: Sees that having partial derivatives is not quite enough.
levels.b: Uses the rule that continuous partial derivatives guarantee it.
levels.c: Studies a counterexample where partials exist but smoothness fails.
levels.d: Connects differentiability to the tangent plane being a good estimate.

VII.11.07.what: The chain rule tracks how changes pass through a chain of dependencies, such as temperature depending on position, which depends on time.

levels.a: Draws tree diagrams showing what depends on what.
levels.b: Applies the chain rule when everything depends on one variable.
levels.c: Applies it when everything depends on two variables.
levels.d: Solves related-rates problems in three dimensions.

VII.11.08.what: Finding slopes of curves or surfaces defined by an equation, without solving for one variable first.

levels.a: Uses the formula for curves given by an equation in x and y.
levels.b: Extends it to surfaces given by an equation in x, y and z.
levels.d: Compares it with the single-variable method learned earlier.

VII.11.09.what: The gradient collects all the partial derivatives into one arrow that points in the steepest uphill direction.

levels.a: Understands the gradient as the vector of partial derivatives.
levels.c: Shows the gradient points straight uphill.
levels.d: Shows its length equals the steepest slope.

VII.11.10.what: A directional derivative measures the rate of change in any chosen direction, like the slope felt walking northeast on a hill.

levels.a: Describes a direction with an arrow of length 1.
levels.b: Computes the rate as the gradient dotted with that direction.
levels.c: Finds the directions of fastest increase and decrease.
levels.d: Interprets directional slopes on a contour map.

VII.11.11.what: The gradient always points at right angles to level curves and level surfaces, straight across the contour lines.

levels.a: Shows the gradient is perpendicular to level curves.
levels.b: Shows it is perpendicular to level surfaces.
levels.c: Finds tangent planes using the gradient.
levels.d: Traces the path of steepest climb up a hill.

VII.11.12.what: A space curve is a path through 3D, like the flight of a drone, described by position over time.

levels.a: Describes a path by position over time and finds its velocity.
levels.b: Finds the length of a curved path.
levels.c: Finds the direction of travel and the direction of turning.
levels.d: Measures how sharply a path bends (its curvature).
